name: Dungan Revolt
native: 陕甘回民起义 (Shǎn-Gān Huímín Qǐyì)
alt: Muslim rebellion in Shaanxi and Gansu

predecessors.name: Qing dynasty
predecessors.text: Hui rebel centres of 1862: Xi'an (besieged by late June 1862), Jinjipu, Hezhou, Xining and Suzhou (Jiuquan)

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: the last Dungan towns, Urumchi and Manas, retaken in August-November 1876

rulers.name: Ma Hualong
rulers.title: fifth leader (jiaozhu) of the Jahriyya, at Jinjipu

ledger.x: 1862: Ma Hualong rises at Jinjipu ('from the beginning of the anti-Qing Muslim Rebellion in 1862').
1862: Ma Zhan'ao launches a movement in Gansu ('no exact date given').
1862: Ma Guiyuan launches a movement in Gansu (no date); the page ties him to Xining through its fall in late 1872, 'its commander, Ma Guiyuan, was captured'.
1862: Ma Wenlu launches a movement in Gansu (no date); 'The city was under the command of Ma Wenlu' at its fall (October 1873).
January 1863: 'In January 1863, Hui forces captured Guyuan.'
August 1863: 'In August 1863, Hui forces captured Pingliang Prefecture.'
October 1863: 'In October 1863, Hui forces captured Ningxia Prefecture' and 'the same month, Ma Hualong's forces attacked Lingzhou' (Qing accounts have them capture it and kill more than 20,000).
February 1864: 'In February 1864, Hui forces captured Weiyuan County.'
3 October 1864: 'On October 3, 1864, the Manchu fortress of Ürümqi also fell to the joint forces of Ürümqi and Kuchean rebels' (the Urumqi rebellion began 26 June 1864).
1869: 'the Hui rebels in Shaanxi fled to Gansu in 1869' after Zuo Zongtang, sent in 1867 and made governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu in 1866, 'defeated the Nian in the province by 1868'.

January 1871: 'Ma Hualong surrendered in January 1871' after the siege of Jinjipu (Dungan page: began September 1870, 'sixteen-month siege'; Ma Hualong page: besieged from July 1869, a year inferred by its footnote, which fits the sixteen months better).

1872: Zuo's 1872 assault on Hezhou was repulsed; then Ma Zhan'ao 'offered to surrender his stronghold' and, per the Ma Zhan'ao page, 'was defected to the Qing Dynasty in 1872' (no month, no place on the Ma Zhan'ao page).
Late 1872: 'Xining fell after a three-month siege in late 1872'; Liu Jintang's campaign began in August 1872 and Ma Guiyuan was captured.
24 October 1873: 'Zuo Zongtang laid siege to Suzhou in September 1873 with 15,000 troops'; 'the city fell on October 24' under Ma Wenlu's command.
August 1876: the Qing 'appeared at Urumchi' and 'the place soon surrendered and the garrison was massacred'; a footnote dates the fall to 18 August.
6 November 1876: the Qing began the siege of Manas on 2 September 1876 and 'on 6 November it surrendered'; the garrison was slaughtered.
November 1876 is the researcher's end of Dungan-held land.

wars.name: Dungan Revolt
wars.outcome: Qing victory: Jinjipu fell in January 1871, Hezhou and Xining in 1872, Suzhou on 24 October 1873 and Urumchi and Manas in August-November 1876; Yaqub Beg's state fell in 1877.

certainty.note: The Dungan page dates sieges and captures but draws no boundaries; every region is a radius or the Ningxia region round a named town.
